Family Sessions

Connection is beautiful

Family

These are the most important people in our lives — our family (and also those who might as well be our family). I want to capture the story of who your family is, so my goal for these sessions is pretty simple: make everyone as comfortable as possible so that they can feel free to be themselves. That way, regardless whether you are all looking at the camera for a more traditional group portrait or candidly enjoying each other’s company, we get to see the genuineness of who your family is.

Locations That Matter

Home is my favorite place to photograph a family. It’s where everyone lets their guard down — where the baby naps, where someone always sits on the same end of the couch, where you actually live. Photographs made there look like your life because they are your life.

But home isn’t the only place that holds something. The trail you walk most Saturdays. The stretch of beach you’ve driven to every summer since the kids were born. Your grandparents’ grove. The field behind the house you’re about to move out of. The gym, the barn, the orange tree someone planted the year your daughter was born. If a place is part of your family’s story, it belongs in these photographs — and years from now it will be the thing that makes you stop scrolling.

So tell me where your family actually spends its time and we’ll go there. Home, somewhere that matters, or both in one session. And if nothing obvious comes to mind, that’s completely normal — I know this area well, and I’ll bring you options worth choosing between.

Legacy

I strive to create images that will serve as a permanent reminder of the emotions, experiences, and relationships shared between you and the people who matter most to you, that can be enjoyed for years to come.

About me

It’s my goal to make photographs that tell your story.

It’s my goal to make photographs that tell your story. I enjoy working with my clients to create images that are genuine and compelling.

The experience

Before the day

We’ll talk before we shoot — where you want to be, what everyone is wearing, and what time of day actually works for your kids. That last one matters more than people expect. A session booked over a nap is a hard session, and I would rather move it than fight it.

For clothes, my advice is the same as it is for everything else here: wear what you already own and feel like yourselves in. Pick one person’s outfit first and build the rest around it. Neutral and natural colors photograph best, and I’d avoid fluorescents, which reflect onto skin, and loud patterns.

Bring whatever is genuinely part of your life right now. The blanket the baby will not sleep without, the dog, the truck, the instrument someone is learning. Those details are what make the photographs yours instead of generic.

The session itself

Here is the part most parents are actually worried about, so let me answer it directly: your kids do not have to behave. They are not going to sit still, they are not going to look at the camera on command, and none of that is a problem I need you to solve for me.

I don’t line people up and count to three. We walk, we talk, I give you something to do rather than a pose to hold, and the photographs happen in between. If a toddler melts down we stop, we let it pass, and we keep going — that is a normal part of the hour, not a thing that ruined it. If someone will not look at me, I photograph them looking at you, which is usually the better frame anyway.

What you get out of that is a set of photographs that look like your family actually is right now, at this age, in this season — not a version of it holding still.

Your gallery

Your gallery lands in your inbox two to three weeks after the session. Full resolution, downloadable, yours to keep, print and share — no watermarks, no per-image fees, and no waiting on prints to find out what you got.

From there you can order prints, books, albums and wall pieces straight from the gallery whenever you want them. Nothing expires on you.

1 Hour Session

1 hour

Built for a family who wants room to breathe — more than one look, time for the kids to forget the camera, and the quiet moments that only turn up once everyone has relaxed.

Why this over the mini. The first ten minutes are the awkward ones for almost everybody. A half hour spends a third of itself getting past that; an hour gets past it and then keeps going, which is where the photographs you actually frame tend to come from.

Built for a family marking something specific — a new baby, a last year at home, a move — who want the house they live in now as well as somewhere open, and a book to hand to grandparents.

Prints & Products. Every session includes the full resolution downloads. From your gallery you’ll have prints, books, albums and other products available at any time — The Year simply builds the album in from the start, designed with you rather than ordered on your own.

Questions

What if my kids won’t cooperate?
They don’t have to. I don’t need anyone to sit still or look at the camera on command, and a meltdown is a normal part of an hour with small children rather than a session ruined. We stop, we let it pass, we keep going. Please don’t spend the week before worrying about this one.
When is the best time to shoot?
Usually the last couple of hours before sunset, when the light is worth having — but with young children the honest answer is whenever they are at their best. Tell me their schedule and we’ll build around it rather than against it.
Where do we shoot?
At home, somewhere outside you all enjoy, or both. Home is my favorite — it’s where everyone lets their guard down. I’m based in the Temecula Valley and shoot across Southern California. Orange County, San Diego and the coast are all regular trips and carry no separate travel fee at these rates.
What should we wear?
Clothes you already own and feel like yourselves in. Pick one person’s outfit first and build around it, keep to neutral and natural colors, and skip fluorescents and loud patterns. I’ll go over it with you before the day.
How long until we see them?
Your gallery arrives two to three weeks after we shoot. If you have a hard deadline — holiday cards, a grandparent’s visit — say so when you book and I’ll tell you honestly whether I can make it.

Next step

Pick the session that fits and send it to me with your name and roughly when you’re hoping to shoot. I’ll come back with dates that work.

A 50% retainer holds your date and comes off the total; the balance is due on the day of your session. I’ll send the contract and the invoice through HoneyBook, so it’s signed and paid in one place. Until the retainer is in, the date stays open to whoever asks next.
